prompt: Valid Anagram: given two strings, return true if one is an anagram of the other.
model_answer:
Same frequency-map idea as word counting. Count each rune in `s`, decrement for each rune in `t`; they're anagrams iff lengths match and every count ends at zero. O(n) time, O(1) extra for a fixed alphabet (or O(k) with a map for Unicode).

Alternative: sort both and compare — O(n log n), simpler but slower. Unicode caveat: iterate runes, not bytes (`strings.Fields`/`[]rune`), which is the same lesson as the word-count project.

prompt: Implement WordCount(s) returning the frequency of each whitespace-separated word. This is your in-app checker challenge.
model_answer:
`strings.Fields` splits on runs of whitespace (handles tabs/newlines/multiple spaces). Loop and increment a `map[string]int`. O(n) over the input.

Interview extensions to be ready for: case-insensitive (lower-case first), strip punctuation, stream very large files with `bufio.Scanner` set to `ScanWords` instead of loading everything into memory, and 'top-K most frequent words' (a heap — Step 2 heaps lesson).

prompt: Once you have word counts, how do you return the K most frequent words efficiently?
model_answer:
Don't fully sort (O(n log n)). Build the count map, then keep a **min-heap of size K**: push each (word,count); if the heap exceeds K, pop the smallest. O(n log K). Or use **bucket sort** by frequency for O(n) when counts are bounded by n.

This is the canonical Top-K pattern (covered in the Step 2 Heaps lesson) and a very common follow-up to any counting problem.
